summary: This bill requires the Comptroller General to complete a full audit of the Federal Reserve Board and banks within 12 months, submit a detailed report to Congress, and repeals existing statutory limits on such audits.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates a GAO audit of the Federal Reserve Board and banks and removes certain statutory audit restrictions. It contains no provisions that authorize, increase, decrease, or restructure any form of government spending. The focus is exclusively on transparency and reporting requirements.
The legislation addresses only Federal Reserve audit procedures and contains no tax-related language, rate changes, or revenue provisions.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market regulation.
The bill is silent on firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the text.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive health services or abortion access.
No defense appropriations, military programs, or national-security spending measures are addressed.
The legislation does not reference environmental regulations, emissions standards, or climate policy.
No welfare, entitlement, or social-services programs are mentioned or altered.
The bill does not address schools, student aid, or education funding.
No drug-enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions exist.
The text contains no sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reforms.
No tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export regulations are included.

While the Federal Reserve influences monetary conditions that can affect debt dynamics, the bill itself only requires an audit and does not direct fiscal policy, deficit targets, or debt-ceiling measures.
No civil-rights, nondiscrimination, or LGBTQ-specific provisions are present.
The bill does not authorize, modify, or restrict any foreign-assistance programs.
No election-administration, voter-access, or campaign-finance language appears.
The legislation addresses neither data privacy nor technology regulation.
No collective-bargaining, worker-protection, or union-related measures are included.
The bill contains no religious-exemption or civil-rights-balancing provisions.
